Power of a group sequential log-rank design

Source: R/ms_power.R
ms_power.Rd

Computes the analysis times, expected events, bounds, stopping probabilities, power and type I error of a design with a given sample size, without simulation.

Usage

ms_power(
  scenario,
  n,
  looks,
  test,
  events = NULL,
  followup = NULL,
  null_scenarios = NULL
)

Arguments

scenario

An ms_scenario object.

n

Total sample size.

looks

An ms_looks object.

test

An ms_test object.

events

Final number of events of the trigger endpoint (for event-driven looks), or final numbers of events named by endpoint ("os", "pfs").

followup

Time from the end of accrual to the final analysis (for an event-driven final look, instead of events).

null_scenarios

For two endpoints, an optional list of ms_scenario objects with the allocation and accrual of scenario, each named by the endpoint ("os" or "pfs") whose null hypothesis is true in the scenario, for example list(os = s_os).

Value

An object of class ms_power, a list with

looks

A data frame with one row per look: time, enrolled, the expected events of the tested endpoint (events, events_control, events_treatment), info_frac, the efficacy bound (z_upper, nominal one-sided p-value p_upper, hazard ratio hr_upper), the futility bound (z_lower, hr_lower), the mean and standard deviation of the statistic (z_mean, z_sd), the probabilities of stopping for efficacy and futility at the look (prob_upper, prob_lower), the cumulative power cum_power, the cumulative alpha spent alpha_spent and the cumulative non-binding type I error cum_alpha. When the looks are driven by another endpoint, events_trigger gives the events of that endpoint.

power

Overall power.

type1

Type I error, non-binding and binding.

n, accrual_duration, study_duration, events

Sample size, accrual duration, calendar time of the final analysis and expected events of the tested endpoint at the final analysis.

settings, scenario, looks_def, test

The inputs.

With two endpoints, looks has one row per endpoint and look at which the endpoint is tested, with the columns above and endpoint, look, trigger and events_trigger (the events of the trigger endpoint at the look, NA for calendar-driven looks); prob_upper is the probability of rejecting the hypothesis of the endpoint at the look under the multiple testing procedure, prob_lower the probability of stopping for futility at the look (first endpoint), cum_power the cumulative sum of prob_upper, alpha_spent the cumulative alpha of the bounds of the endpoint and cum_alpha the cumulative non-binding probability of rejecting the hypothesis of the endpoint under the global null hypothesis. power has the powers of the two endpoints (named by endpoint), the probability of rejecting both hypotheses (both) and of rejecting at least one (any); type1 is the familywise error rate under the global null hypothesis, non-binding and binding; fwer is a data frame with the familywise error rate under the global null hypothesis and under each scenario of null_scenarios; events has the expected events of each endpoint at its last look; final_events the final numbers of events of the trigger endpoints; and mean and sigma are the mean vector and covariance matrix of the statistics in the order of the rows of looks.

Details

For event-driven looks, the final analysis takes place when the expected number of events of the trigger endpoint reaches events, or at followup after the end of accrual. The interim analyses take place when the expected number of events reaches the fractions given in looks. For calendar-driven looks, events and followup are not used.

At each look, the standardized log-rank statistics have the mean and covariance of lr_cov with the approximations chosen in test. The bounds are computed by gs_bounds and the stopping probabilities by gs_prob. The power is the probability of crossing an efficacy bound when the futility bounds are applied. The type I error is computed under ms_null applied to the scenario, with event-driven looks at the same numbers of events of the trigger endpoint; the non-binding value ignores the futility bounds and the binding value applies them.

The hazard ratios at the bounds are exp(-z / sqrt(p0 p1 d)), where d is the expected number of events of the tested endpoint.

When the looks have different triggers (see ms_looks), each trigger endpoint has its own final number of events, and a look driven by it takes place when its expected number of events reaches the fraction of the look times that number. The final numbers are given by events, named by endpoint when the looks are driven by the events of two endpoints, for example c(pfs = 300, os = 250). With followup, or without events when the final look is calendar-driven, they are the expected numbers of events at the final analysis; the looks driven by an endpoint other than that of the final look then need fractions below 1.

With two endpoints (test from ms_test with two endpoints), the statistics of the two endpoints at the looks at which they are tested have the joint distribution of lr_cov, with the observed events of the trigger endpoints determining the event-driven looks for variance = "studentized". Each endpoint has its own bounds, and the rejection probabilities under the multiple testing procedure are computed by gs_prob_mtp. The familywise error rate is computed under ms_null applied to the scenario (the global null hypothesis), where the correlations between the endpoints are those of Danzer et al. (2025, Theorem 1), and under each scenario of null_scenarios, where the hypothesis of one endpoint is true and that of the other is not (a partial null hypothesis). Such scenarios cannot be derived from the multistate model of the design scenario and are given by the user, for example a model with the same OS in both groups and a difference in PFS. Under each null scenario the event-driven looks take place at the same numbers of events of their trigger endpoints.

References

Danzer MF, Rufibach K, Beyersmann J, Schmidt R (2025). Exhausting the type I error level in event-driven group-sequential designs with a closed testing procedure for progression-free and overall survival. arXiv:2512.08658.

See also

ms_size, ms_looks, ms_test, gs_prob_mtp

Examples

ctl <- ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
trt <- ms_model(death = 0.7 * log(2) / 12)
scn <- ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 20))
ms_power(scn, n = 400, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 1)),
         test = ms_test(), events = 300)
#> Group sequential log-rank design
#>   Tested endpoint: OS; looks driven by OS events
#>   Sample size: 400; accrual duration: 20; final analysis at: 39.67
#>   Power: 0.8689
#>   Type I error: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.025 (binding)
#>  look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower hr_lower
#>     1 20.47    150       0.5   2.963 0.001525   0.6164    -Inf       NA
#>     2 39.67    300       1.0   1.969 0.024500   0.7967   1.969   0.7967
#>  prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>      0.2158     0.0000    0.2158
#>      0.6531     0.1311    0.8689

# PFS first, then OS: final PFS analysis at 300 PFS events with an OS
# interim analysis, final OS analysis at 220 OS events
fl <- ms_scenario(ms_fleischer(4, 12), ms_fleischer(6, 16),
                  accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25))
lk <- ms_looks(c("pfs", "os"), fraction = c(1, 1), test = list(c("pfs", "os"), "os"))
ms_power(fl, n = 450, looks = lk,
         test = ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), mtp = "fixed_sequence"),
         events = c(pfs = 300, os = 220))
#> Group sequential log-rank design with two endpoints
#>   Endpoints: PFS, then OS (fixed sequence, overall); looks driven by PFS events and OS events
#>   Sample size: 450; accrual duration: 18; final analysis at: 23.05
#>   Power: PFS 0.9387, OS 0.5452; both 0.5452; at least one 0.9387
#>   FWER under global null: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.025 (binding)
#>  endpoint look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower
#>       PFS    1 18.62    300    1.0000   1.960 0.025000   0.7975   1.960
#>        OS    1 18.62    163    0.7407   2.357 0.009207   0.6912    -Inf
#>        OS    2 23.05    220    1.0000   2.009 0.022243   0.7626   2.009
#>  hr_lower prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>    0.7975     0.9387          0    0.9387
#>        NA     0.2966          0    0.2966
#>    0.7626     0.2486          0    0.5452
